root_idea.summary: The root centers on the number five and its relations: five as a count, a fifth position, and one part out of five.
root_idea.development: From the numerical core, the lexical field extends to taking or dividing into fifths, becoming or making a group five, fifth-day watering cycles, five-unit measurements, and conventional terms associated with five.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic feminine form is normalized under the masculine ordinal citation form خَامِس.
Distinct cardinal numeral meaning: fifty; the Quranic form is the inflected form خَمْسِينَ.
Distinct fractional noun meaning: one fifth or a fifth part.

senses.definition: Fifth; occupying the fifth position in an ordered series.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quranic occurrences use the feminine form خَامِسَةُ/خَامِسَةَ in the reciprocal-oath construction of 24:7 and 24:9.
A cardinal numeral used with counted nouns and as a standalone count.
The Quranic occurrences use the oblique form خَمْسِينَ.

senses.definition: One fifth; a fifth part or share of a whole.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quranic occurrence, it denotes one fifth of the spoils, with the pronoun referring back to them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a fifth part of people's possessions or of property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action is also described as taking one from five, especially in the division of spoil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be fifth among a group, or to make a group five by joining it; by extension, to complete a count such as fourteen to fifteen or forty-nine to fifty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be a member entering a group or the agent who completes its number.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a rope of five strands twisted together.
Of camels, to drink on the fifth day in the watering cycle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The day-counting convention is the one specified in the lexical discussion of the fifth-day watering schedule.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something five.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the causative Form II use of making an object or quantity five.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To divide something into five fifths.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the partitioning use, distinct from merely making a count reach five.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something five-cornered, five-angled, or pentagonal.
Of a female, to give birth to her fifth offspring.
To remain five nights with someone, or to perform an action for a five-unit period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited construction is used with a wife, but the source extends the expression to other actions and relations without restricting its object to that example.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fifth-day watering of land or seed-produce in a watering cycle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is the watering that follows the tarbīʿ, or fourth-day watering, in the stated agricultural schedule.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a group, to become five or fifty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two numerical values are recorded as related intransitive uses of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be associated with a fifth-day camel-watering schedule.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man whose camels come to water on the fifth day, under the stated counting convention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fifth-day watering interval of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources record variant explanations of whether the preceding watering day is included in the count.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert, journey, or route in which water is reached only after a fifth-day interval.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe a long waterless passage or a journey in which camels are watered only at the beginning and end of the interval.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To use a pretext, pretend one thing while intending another, or proceed by artifice toward a concealed aim.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional proverb based on advancing camels from a fifth-day to a sixth-day watering schedule.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fifth young one or offspring.
A Yemeni garment of the burd type.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained either by the name of an early Yemeni maker or by association with the numerical root; a variant form is also reported in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To direct one's five senses toward all six directions, concentrating one's thoughts and attention on an investigation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic extension of the numerical expression, with the six directions understood as above, below, before, behind, right, and left.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fifteen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A compound cardinal numeral with the masculine counted-noun pattern; the corresponding feminine form is also recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fiftieth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An ordinal use in addition to the cardinal meaning fifty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In groups of five; five at a time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distributive adverbial expression, as in people arriving five and five together or successively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An army or military host.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained as an army arranged in five divisions, as associated with fifth-share distribution, or as a heavily armed host; these are explanations of the same military designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thursday, the fifth day of the week.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is used independently or in the phrase يَوْمُ الخَمِيسِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or group of men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression asking what company of men someone belongs to.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Measuring five spans; especially, a growing boy who is five spans in height and has not reached full stature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In other applications, the adjective may denote something that reaches or consists of five; the boy-specific use is explicitly limited to the stated stage of growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In grammatical terminology, a word composed of five letters, whether all are radicals or some are augmentative.
A person who fasts alone on Thursday.
Fifteenth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A compound ordinal numeral with masculine and feminine variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, adhering to a fifth-day watering schedule.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is applied to camels that drink on the fifth day or pasture for three days before returning to water under the alternative count described in the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Five-cornered, five-angled, or pentagonal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective or noun for a thing having five corners or angles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Five cubits in length, applied especially to a spear or to a garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same measurement may be used of a small garment or cloth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Near together and in a state of agreement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiom imagining two people fitting together within a five-cubit garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rope made of five strands twisted together.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Feminine grammatical cross-reference only; no independent lexical branch.
The fifth-part meaning is represented by the Quranic fractional sense.
The cardinal meaning, including ordinary counted objects, is represented by the Quranic sense.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the final meaning of خِمْس.
The ordinal meaning is represented under the normalized public citation form خَامِس.

cautions: The Quranic cardinal, ordinal, and fractional forms are distinct: خَمْسَة is five, خَامِسَة is fifth, and خُمُس is one fifth.
The classical descriptions of خِمْس and related camel-watering terms preserve variant conventions for counting the watering days.
